# `Q-2-50` — Doubled curly braces are not supported

> Quarto 2 does not treat doubled curly braces (`{{...}}`) as an
> escape. To write literal braces in text, escape each brace as
> `\{...\}` or use a code span.

## What this means

Quarto 1 (and RMarkdown/knitr before it) used doubled curly braces as
an escape: writing a code cell header as `{{python}}` *displayed* the
cell — with single braces — instead of running it. Quarto 2 does not
have this escape, in either place it used to appear:

- **In prose**, `{{python}}` is a parse error (this error). Curly
  braces are reserved for attribute syntax (see
  [`Q-2-41`](Q-2-41.qmd)), and doubling them does not escape them.
- **In a code fence header**, ```` ```{{python}} ```` is not an
  executable cell and not an escape: the fence renders as a literal
  code block whose language reads `{{python}}`, and Quarto 2 reports
  this error so the doubled braces don't silently end up in your
  output.

## Why this happens

- **Porting documents from Quarto 1.** Documentation *about* Quarto —
  pages that show readers how to write executable cells — commonly
  uses the Quarto 1 escape ```` ```{{python}} ```` to display a cell.
  This is by far the most common source.
- **Template languages in prose.** Text that quotes Jinja, Mustache,
  or GitHub Actions expressions (`{{ expr }}`) outside a code block
  hits the same parse error.

## How to fix

**To display a code cell** (the Quarto 1 `{{...}}` use case): wrap
the cell in a fenced code block with more backticks, and write the
cell with **single** braces. Fenced code blocks are displayed
verbatim in Quarto 2, so no escape is needed:

`````markdown
````markdown
```{python}
1 + 1
```
````
`````

This shows the reader exactly what they should type.

**To write literal braces in prose**, escape each brace, or use a
code span:

```markdown
the pipeline interpolates \{\{ .Release.Name \}\} at deploy time.
the pipeline interpolates `{{ .Release.Name }}` at deploy time.
```

**To run the cell**, write single braces: ```` ```{python} ````.

Note that doubled braces *inside* a code block's body need no change
at all — fence bodies are verbatim, so a code block quoting a Jinja
template keeps its `{{ expr }}` exactly as written. (This is also why
Quarto 2 dropped the Quarto 1 escape rather than collapsing doubled
braces everywhere: collapsing would corrupt code blocks that genuinely
mean `{{`.)

## Example

Bad input (Quarto 1 idiom):

`````markdown
```{{python}}
1 + 1
```
`````

Corrected (display the cell):

`````markdown
````markdown
```{python}
1 + 1
```
````
`````

Corrected (run the cell):

`````markdown
```{python}
1 + 1
```
`````
